**5B.7 Research Note**
Overall: **mostly evidence-based and reform-oriented, but not cleanly technocratic.** The 2024 record shows repeated reliance on IMF/World Bank diagnostics, explicit correction of macro mistakes, and some concrete follow-through. The main counterevidence is that Sharif still kept a highly personal, PM-centered grip on parts of economic policy, with some loyalist-heavy cabinet structure and limited proof of genuine institutional autonomy.

- **Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility**; Publisher: IMF; Date: 2024-07-12; URL: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff; Claim: the program explicitly grounded policy in diagnosis and correction, calling for broadening the tax base, improving SOE management, strengthening competition, phasing out distortive incentives, and advancing governance/anti-corruption reforms. This is the strongest evidence that Sharif’s 2024 economic policy was based on evidence and correction rather than slogans. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`.

- **Pakistan: Second and Final Review Under the Stand-By Arrangement**; Publisher: IMF; Date: 2024-05-10; URL: https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/10/pakistan-second-and-final-review-under-the-stand-by-arrangement-press-release-staff-report-548741; Claim: the IMF said sustainable recovery required strict fiscal targets, a market-determined exchange rate, better tax collection, SOE reform, and governance/anti-corruption measures, with inclusive growth and job creation still dependent on continued structural reform. That is strong evidence of policy driven by evidence and error-correction, not denial. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`.

- **IMF Executive Board Concludes 2024 Article IV Consultation for Pakistan and Approves 37-month Extended Arrangement**; Publisher: IMF; Date: 2024-09-27; URL: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr; Claim: the IMF described the new program as entrenching macro stability, strengthening competition, removing state distortions, improving the FDI regime, reforming SOEs, and supporting a fairer business environment. It also noted how incomplete the reform agenda remained, which makes this evidence for evidence-based policy but not for full success. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`.

- **Pakistan PM unveils broader plan to sell most state-owned firms**; Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint; Date: 2024-05-14; URL: https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-unveils-broader-plan-to-sell-most-state-owned-firms/2084587/; Claim: Sharif said most SOEs would be privatized except strategic ones, framing it as a fiscal repair and taxpayer-savings measure. This is concrete correction of prior policy mistakes, not just rhetoric, though it still reads as top-down executive management. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`.

- **Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says**; Publisher: Reuters via Dawn; Date: 2024-10-10; URL: https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298; Claim: the government renegotiated power-purchase contracts to reduce tariffs and save about Rs60 billion per year. This is one of the clearest examples of policy correction based on cost evidence rather than denial or slogan-driven inertia. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.6`.

- **Pakistan PM to choose banker Aurangzeb as finance minister, sources say**; Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint; Date: 2024-03-11; URL: https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-to-choose-banker-aurangzeb-as-finance-minister-sources-say/1996592/; Claim: Sharif chose Muhammad Aurangzeb, a career banker, over veteran political operators to run finance. That supports an evidence-based reading because he picked a technocrat for a diagnosis-heavy macro fix, not a pure patronage appointment. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.2`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`.

- **PM forms new Economic Advisory Council for policy guidance**; Publisher: The News; Date: 2024-05-19; URL: https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/1190715-pm-forms-new-economic-advisory-council-without-dar-aurangzeb; Claim: Sharif created an advisory council with economists, technocrats, and business figures specifically to guide policy. This supports consultation-based policymaking and some correction of mistakes through expertise. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.2`, `5B.6`.

- **PM takes charge of ECNEC, sidelining finance minister**; Publisher: Dawn; Date: 2024-06-15; URL: https://www.dawn.com/news/1839967; Claim: Sharif personally took charge of ECNEC rather than leaving it to finance minister Aurangzeb. This is the clearest counterevidence to a fully evidence-led model because it suggests continued personalization and PM-centered control rather than trust in delegated technocratic management. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.2`, `5B.6`.

- **Cabinet details reveal mix of technocrat and old guard**; Publisher: Dawn; Date: 2024-03-12; URL: https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1820930; Claim: the cabinet mixed a new finance technocrat with old-guard figures such as Ishaq Dar and other loyalists. This weakens the clean “correction over patronage” reading because it shows reform coexisting with political accommodation. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.2`, `5B.5`.

- **Pakistan PM Sharif picks prominent banker in new cabinet, document shows**; Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint; Date: 2024-03-11; URL: https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-sharif-picks-prominent-banker-in-new-cabinet-document-shows/1996146/; Claim: Reuters noted the banker appointment was made from Sharif’s office, which supports competence but also shows top-down control rather than autonomous institutional policymaking. That is a mild negative on the “evidence, not patronage” dimension because the reform path was still personally managed. QIDs: `5B.7`, `5B.2`, `5B.6`.

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of explicit self-correction after a named economic failure, nor much direct evidence of scapegoating in economic policy speeches.
- The clearest pattern is: **policy content was evidence-heavy and IMF/World Bank-driven, but implementation remained PM-centered and only partly insulated from political patronage.**
